name: Democratic Socialism
summary: Democratic socialism aims to replace capitalism with an economy under democratic social, cooperative and public ownership and control, and insists that socialism and democracy cannot be separated. The branches reviewed share public or workforce ownership of key sectors, democratic planning or control of the economy, strong unions, progressive taxation, universal welfare, anti-militarism, secular states and rejection of one-party rule. They differ on basic income, central planning, NATO, the EU and Israel.
scope: A family entry answering only what several independent branches share: Die Linke (Germany, Erfurt Programme 2011), Enhedslisten (Denmark, principle programme 2014, Danish), SV (Norway, principle programme 2023, Nynorsk), PSOL (Brazil, programme page, Portuguese), and US democratic socialism treated as one branch (Socialist Party USA national platform and a DSA chapter platform; DSA's national site was blocked), plus Rosa Luxemburg's democratic critique of Bolshevism and the Stanford Encyclopedia on socialist ideals. Social democracy, market socialism, libertarian socialism, Eurocommunism and Marxism-Leninism have their own entries. A position needs two or more independent branches; high needs four or more; single-branch positions are null and opposite positions are 0, low.

universal-healthcare.rationale: Die Linke wants health care guaranteed to all, the US parties single-payer or free universal care, SV a non-commercial public welfare system and PSOL an uncompromising defence of Brazil's public health system SUS.

raise-minimum-wage.rationale: Die Linke demands a statutory minimum wage tied to the national average and the US parties $20 to $25 an hour, indexed.

markets-allocate-better.rationale: Die Linke, Enhedslisten and PSOL all call for democratic regulation or planning of production in place of profit-driven market allocation, though none abolishes markets outright.

public-ownership.rationale: Die Linke wants more public ownership of utilities and finance, Enhedslisten public bodies owning and running enterprises, SV public and cooperative ownership, PSOL social control of production, and the US parties public ownership of key industries.

tax-the-wealthy.rationale: Die Linke demands a millionaires' tax, the US parties steeply graduated income and estate taxes, SV a redistributive tax system and PSOL progressive taxation.

unions-good.rationale: Die Linke calls strong unions necessary, SV calls them decisive in a socialist society, Enhedslisten ties workplace organising to socialism, PSOL condemns union weakening, and the US parties defend the right to organise.

property-fundamental.rationale: Die Linke cites the Basic Law that means of production may become common property, Enhedslisten demands fundamental changes in property rights over production, and PSOL calls for expropriating unproductive estates.

regulate-corporations.rationale: Die Linke wants strict competition control of business and SV wants regulation of technology giants and democratic control of the economy.

cut-welfare.rationale: All the branches defend and expand public welfare: Die Linke wants Hartz IV abolished, SV a non-commercial welfare state, Enhedslisten collective welfare as a gain, PSOL the SUS, and the US parties full-income benefits.

worker-ownership.rationale: Die Linke lists workforce ownership, Enhedslisten employees' ownership and SV worker-owned firms, each as one form alongside public and cooperative ownership.

surveillance-ok.rationale: Die Linke opposes the surveillance state, the Socialist Party USA would repeal the PATRIOT Act, and SV warns surveillance and liberty restrictions risk abuse of power against marginalised groups.
